name: Düsseldorf School
summary: Large, cool, frontal colour pictures of buildings, rooms, crowds and landscapes in fine detail. The method comes from the Bechers' typologies, and the scale comes from the museum wall.

philosophy.core_thesis: Seen without drama and in great detail, an ordinary place becomes a map of the way we live.
design_principles: Use a 4×5 in or digital medium format camera, with a lens of 90mm to 150mm.
Photograph in flat grey light with a shadow ratio of 1.5:1 or less, and with no people posed.
Keep the camera level and square to the subject, so that verticals stay vertical.
Use a viewpoint raised by 3 to 20m, or a straight-on view at 1.5m, and hold it for the whole series.
Print large: 1.5m to 3m on the long edge, with sharpness from edge to edge.
Work in series of 20 or more, so that the type is the subject.
anti_patterns: Picturesque framing that invites a story
One-off hero images with no series

composition.framing: Frontal and complete; the subject sits whole in the frame with a margin of sky or ground.
composition.viewpoint: Level, often raised by 3 to 20m; the camera sits square to the plane of the subject.
composition.geometry: A grid of windows, shelves, boxes or people; repeats make the picture.
composition.subject_placement: Centred or on a strict grid line, with a margin of 10–25% on each side.

principles.rule: Set the main axis at 0.5 of the width, within 0.02.
Repeat a window, shelf or figure at one constant pitch, with 12 to 60 repeats in the frame.
Keep the 4:5 or 5:4 ratio of the plate, with no crop.
Leave 10–25% of the frame as sky or ground.
Hold one distance, one height and one light across 20 to 100 prints.

light.quality: Flat, soft and overcast: no cast shadow edges.
light.time_of_day: Midday under an even grey sky

lens_and_camera.format: 4×5 in or 8×10 in sheet film; digital medium format at 100 megapixels
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus at one third into the scene; the depth of field covers the full subject.
equipment: view camera or medium format camera

colour_and_grade.treatment: Neutral colour, slightly cool, with no creative grade; the surfaces keep their local tint.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 6500K, tint 0.
Set the black point at 3% and the white point at 96%.
Apply +5% midtone contrast, and no more.
Reduce saturation by 5% overall and keep local hues exact.
Correct lens vertical and horizontal lines to 0°.
Add no grain, no vignette and no sharpening halo.
colour_and_grade.grain: None: fine detail, sharp across the whole plate

subject_and_staging.staging: Minimal. The maker picks the place, the hour and the grey light, and then removes the weather and the anecdote.
subject_and_staging.direction: For a portrait: a neutral face, a straight stance and a grey ground; no smile.

workflow: Scan the sheet at 4000 dpi or capture at the sensor's base ISO.
Correct geometry to 0° and colour to neutral grey.
Print as a C-type or pigment print on a face-mounted sheet, 1.5 to 3m wide.
Hang as a grid of one type with 6 to 20 prints.
post_processing.output: A very large, sharp colour print or a grid of typology prints.

emotion.target_response: Detached awe: the viewer is calm and sees a pattern in an ordinary scene.

use_cases: annual-report imagery with a cool authority
image prompts for flat, frontal, grid-based scenes
avoid_when: The brief needs a hero moment, warm light or a person with a story.
The final size is small, where the detail is lost.

modifiers.how: Use a 35mm or 6×7 camera at 1–3m, in saturated slide film at ISO 100, in warm low sun with a close subject.
Go back to black and white at 4×5, f/32, with no person in the frame; keep the 4:5 ratio and the low sun at 15° elevation.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 90 to 150 mm on 4×5 in.
